$comment: Bash commands refused before they run, shared by every harness.
The list is deliberately SHORT and high-confidence: only commands that are
unrecoverable or violate standing policy, never everyday operations. A guard
that blocks correct work gets switched off, and then it protects nothing.
Regexes are stored in the Python-JavaScript intersection (no named groups, no
verbose mode, lookaheads only) and every pattern here is compile-checked
Consumers: pi/extensions/bash-guard.ts (tool_call) and the dsh guard plugin
(tools/pre-execute). Claude covers part of this ground with permissions.deny
in claude/settings.json, which is glob-shaped rather than regex and so cannot
be generated from here — it is maintained alongside, not derived.

deny_bash.label: recursive force-delete of a catastrophic target
deny_bash.reason: Blocked: recursive force-delete of root, home, or * is unrecoverable. Delete a specific scoped path instead.
deny_bash.note: `rm` must sit at a command position (start, after ;&|( or newline, or behind sudo/doas) so a mention inside a grep/echo string literal is not blocked. The target matches as a whole shell word ANYWHERE in the arg list, so a trailing redirect, comment, flag-after-target, `--`, or quotes cannot slip past. Scoped paths (/home, ./build, ~/.cache) are deliberately allowed.

deny_bash.label: bare git force-push
deny_bash.reason: Blocked by policy: bare force-push overwrites remote history. Use `git push --force-with-lease` after explicit user confirmation.
deny_bash.note: `--force-with-lease` is deliberately allowed. Global options (-C dir, -c cfg, --git-dir=) between `git` and `push` are tolerated, but the gap only matches option-shaped tokens so a bare word cannot let the match walk into quoted prose. The lookahead classes exclude \n\r so a --force-with-lease on a LATER line cannot exempt an earlier bare force.

deny_bash.label: git push with a + refspec (force with no flag)
deny_bash.reason: Blocked by policy: a leading `+` on a refspec force-overwrites the remote ref. Use `git push --force-with-lease` after explicit user confirmation.
deny_bash.note: Force with no --force flag, so the flag-based rule above never sees it.

deny_bash.label: raw write to a block device (dd of=/dev/…, mkfs)
deny_bash.reason: Blocked: raw writes to block devices destroy the disk. If this is genuinely intended, the user must run it themselves.
deny_bash.note: Flags between mkfs and the device, quoted `of=` targets, backslash line-continuations, and macOS disk/rdisk names are all covered.

deny_bash.label: world-writable chmod
deny_bash.reason: Blocked by policy: chmod 777 makes a path world-writable. Grant the narrowest mode that works (755 for dirs, 644 for files, +x for scripts).
deny_bash.note: Scoped modes (chmod 755, chmod +x) are deliberately untouched; only the everyone-can-write bit is refused. Mirrors the Bash(chmod 777:*) entries in claude/settings.json.

deny_bash.label: publish to a package registry
deny_bash.reason: Blocked by policy: publishing is not reversible. If a release is genuinely intended, the user runs it themselves.
deny_bash.note: `(?![\w-])` rather than \b: a word boundary sits between "publish" and the hyphen in `npm publish-please`, a different and legitimate tool.
